text:
Alyssa: Heads-up — noticed a chunk of route evaluation traces are missing the header-override transitions in prod for requests that hit the gateway with X-Route-Priority. Console shows the request matched the canary rule but the trace doesn't show the override step. Anyone seen this? :thinking:

Sid: I saw something similar earlier in staging. The rule evaluator log shows a "header_normalize" hook, but the trace sampler sometimes drops those spans. Could be sampling or tag filtering.

Jamie: @Sid can you paste the trace id? We can grep request logs and cross-reference. Also, did deploy-bot push any route changes yesterday?

Alyssa: Trace id: trace-0x9f3b2 (copied from trace UI). Sampled spans in the trace are: evaluator.match -> route.select. Missing: evaluator.override.header-normalize. Logs for that request show header rewrite: `X-Route-Priority: canary` -> `route_priority_override=canary`.

Sid: Repro steps I used in staging: curl -v with header and check /internal/route-trace. Example:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Route-Priority: canary" \\n  https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/route_check -d '{"input":"test"}'
```

When sampling is at 100% in staging I see all steps. With default 5% sampler the header-normalize span is frequently dropped.

Marta: UI nuance: when a header override is applied by the gateway we surface it as a decorated row under the route in the Console rollout view. But if the trace lacks that span the rollout UX still shows the canary match and the trace link looks inconsistent. I think that's what Alyssa is seeing.

Jamie: infra-bot shows a config push at 2026-03-15 03:12 UTC that bumped decision-trace-sample-rate to 0.05 globally (for cost reasons). deploy-bot also did a config sync at 03:20. @Marta this might explain the mismatch in prod but not staging.

infra-bot: config-change: decision-trace-sample-rate set to 0.05 for namespace=prod by ops/telemetry (reason: lower ingest).

Sid: Two hypotheses: 1) sampling is uniform at span-level and small spans (header-normalize) have lower retention; 2) the evaluator marks override spans as low-priority, so sampler drops them first. We have code that marks "meta" spans with priority=low for noise reduction.

Alyssa: Could we change sampling to preserve all spans tied to rule-eval flows (maybe attach eval_id and always keep spans with eval_id)? That would keep rollouts UI consistent.

Marta: We already have a feature flag to force-keep spans if span.attributes.eval_id exists, but console doesn't always set that attribute because some gateway layers normalize headers before the eval_id injection. Race condition.

Jamie: Practical short-term: increase decision-trace-sample-rate to 0.2 for the canary namespace or ramp for the last 48h window for forensic. Long-term: ensure eval_id is injected earlier (at ingress) before header normalization.

Sid: Agreed. I can open a quick PR to inject eval_id at the earliest gateway hook. Will also add a sampler rule: keep spans where attributes contains route.override.* or eval_id.

Alyssa: Thanks. Forensics request: can we retroactively stitch traces using request_id if trace spans are missing? We have request logs with request_id and evaluator logs with same id but no spans.

Jamie: We can do a best-effort join using request_id and a synthetic "inferred" span in trace explorer that points to the log entry. Not perfect but helps triage. I'll run a job to backfill for trace-0x9f3b2 and similar in the last 12h.

Marta: UX follow-up: I'll add a console note for rollouts that if trace sampling is low, the "override" row may be hidden and the trace link could be misleading (:warning:). Also adding a small banner when sample-rate < 10%.

Sid: Plan: 1) hotfix PR to inject eval_id at ingress (sid/route-inject-evalid) 2) sampler change to keep override spans (sid/sampler-keep-override) 3) temporary increase sample rate for prod-canary namespace to 20% for 6 hours (ops). 4) Jamie runs backfill.

deploy-bot: scheduled: increase decision-trace-sample-rate to 0.2 for namespace=prod-canary at 2026-03-16T09:30:00Z (by ops).

Alyssa: If someone can own postmortem notes listing tradeoffs (ingest cost vs debugability) I'll draft the doc. Also want telemetry to expose metric: missing-eval-span-rate per route.

Jamie: I'll own the postmortem. Assigning to myself.

Alyssa: Thanks all. If you see more missing traces please drop trace ids here. :thumbsup:
